claim: Retrieving a few similar solved cases (or distilled strategies) improves LLM agents over no memory in 7 independent agent papers; typical gain is 4 to 19 points on agentic tasks (Memento +6.7 F1 DeepResearcher, ExpeL +19 ALFWorld for the full method and +15 for retrieval-only, Sarukkai +16 ALFWorld, ReasoningBank +8.3 WebArena, AWM +12.0 WebArena, DS-Agent, Agent KB +6.1 GAIA at pass@1 and +5.5 at pass@3 against a matched baseline; its headline +18.7 compares pass@3 with a pass@1 baseline).
agent_test: Run the same solver with and without a case library on held-out tasks, same total tokens including retrieved text.
audit_note: Agent KB's +18.7 compares Agent KB at pass@3 (73.9) with the baseline at pass@1 (55.2); like for like it is +6.1 at pass@1 (55.2 to 61.2) and +5.5 at pass@3 (68.5 to 73.9). ExpeL +19 is the full method (retrieval-only is 55 vs ReAct 40, +15). Other figures (Memento +6.7 F1, Sarukkai +16, ReasoningBank +8.3, AWM +12.0, DS-Agent) check out.
claim_before_audit: Retrieving a few similar solved cases improves LLM agents over no memory, in 7+ independent agent papers; typical gain is 4 to 19 points on agentic tasks (Memento +6.7 F1 DeepResearcher, ExpeL +19 ALFWorld, Sarukkai +16 ALFWorld, ReasoningBank +8.3 WebArena, AWM +12.0 WebArena, DS-Agent, Agent KB +18.7 GAIA pass@3).

claim: Few retrieved cases are best. Memento peaks at K=4 (64.5 F1, 78.5 PM) against K=1 63.6/77.9 and K=32 63.9/78.1 (re-verified in the paper table); DS-Agent finds one case best; Sarukkai uses k=6. Beyond that, more cases give no gain and sometimes a loss. Gap search: OBAM retrieval of 1 case loses 7-8 points and saturates at 5; Bertsch 2025 retrieval advantage over random falls from 51.5 to 4.9 points as demonstrations go from 1 to 1,500.
agent_test: Sweep k = 0,1,2,4,8 at equal context budget; plot success against tokens.
audit_note: Minor: DS-Agent's 'one case best' is the authors' statement that more cases interfere; OBAM shows the opposite shape for its own region-retrieval (1 case worse than 5, saturating at 5), which the claim already notes.

claim: In Memento, adding CBR gave +3.7 to +6.7 F1 (HLE +4.5, SimpleQA +3.7, DeepResearcher +6.7); planning without CBR gave +11.0 to +32.5 F1 on the same sets. In Dynamic Cheatsheet an empty-memory scaffold already moved Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 from 23.3 to 36.7 before any cases.
agent_test: Always include a scaffold-only arm with an empty case library; credit memory only for the difference.
audit_note: Memento's CBR increment on F1 is +3.7 (SimpleQA) to +6.7 (DeepResearcher), with HLE +4.5, so the stated +4.5 to +6.7 leaves out SimpleQA +3.7; planning without CBR (+11.0 to +32.5 F1) and the Dynamic Cheatsheet 23.3 to 36.7 empty-scaffold figures are right.
claim_before_audit: The CBR increment is smaller than the gain from planning or scaffolding alone. In Memento, adding CBR gave +4.5 to +6.7 F1; planning without CBR gave +11.0 to +32.5 F1 on the same sets. In Dynamic Cheatsheet an empty-memory scaffold already moved Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 from 23.3 to 36.7 before any cases.

claim: Part of the apparent learning curve in case-memory studies is not from cases. Memento: the no-CBR baseline rose 78.65 to 84.47 over five passes; the CBR gap at pass 5 was only +0.38 (non-parametric) and +0.97 (parametric).
agent_test: Use a repeat-pass control with memory disabled.

claim: Retaining everything is worse than retaining selectively. Xiong 2025: add-all 55.48/13.05/32.32/59.90 against strict filter 70.95/38.50/51.00/85.40 on four agents (RegAgent/EHRAgent/AgentDriver/CIC-IoT); add-all fell below a fixed human-curated memory (67.53/16.75/40.11/71.50) on all four. Classical IB2 vs IB3 agree in direction.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare retain-all, retain-passed-by-judge, and retain-nothing across a task stream.
audit_note: Minor: Xiong's fixed-memory baseline is a subset of training runs with correct execution, not described as human-curated (only the strict filter is human-evaluated); Aha 1991 IB2 vs IB3 numbers match Table 6.

claim: The quality of the retain filter decides the outcome. A weak LLM judge adds errors that spread (gap to error-free memory grows); a judge fine-tuned on only 300 trajectories (C3) beat add-all on all four agents; a noisy deletion judge hurt (CIC-IoT 74.00 to 68.80). Gap search: a same-model judge of graph-colouring answers accepted 30 of 500 candidates and was right 5 times (precision about 17%), and a self-critique loop scored 1 of 100 against a 16% baseline (Stechly 2023). The minimum useful judge precision is still unmeasured.
agent_test: Measure judge precision on our own pass/fail labels before using it to gate retention.
audit_note: Minor: 68.80 for CIC-IoT is Xiong's combined (periodic plus history-based) deletion under the coarse judge; history-based alone gave 73.70, periodic alone 78.10, and coarse deletion helped EHRAgent (25.91 to 33.55), so 'noisy deletion judge hurt' is one cherry-picked cell. The 300 are described as correct judge data points.

claim: Agents copy retrieved cases: output similarity rises with input similarity, so a wrong stored case misleads later tasks. Gap search: harm from a retrieved case is concentrated on hard items (Raw memory across tasks -26.1 points on items the agent had failed alone) and is worst when the distractor shares topic or roles with the problem (63.1 vs 80.7).
agent_test: Count harm cases (retrieved case present and answer worse than the no-memory run).
audit_note: Minor: the 63.1 vs 80.7 figure is from Shi 2023 irrelevant sentences inserted into math problems (code-davinci-002), applied here by analogy to retrieved cases; Hu 2026 -26.1 is one ALFWorld transfer pair (n=46 hard items).

claim: Deleting low-utility cases can help when the utility signal is reliable: strict-evaluator history-based deletion EHRAgent 38.67 to 42.06 (memory 1012 to 784), CIC-IoT 85.40 to 89.60 (904 to 788), but combined deletion on RegAgent 70.95 to 66.58.
agent_test: Test pruning at fixed memory size; report both score and size.

claim: Competence-preserving deletion (footprint) held 100% competence where random fell to 86% and utility-based to 80% in a 50-case property-valuation base; a follow-up found footprint sensitive to noise. Smyth and Keane numbers were not re-opened in the cross-check; small, old domain.
agent_test: Compare random, recency and coverage-based deletion on our class record; include noisy cases.

claim: Storing only cases the memory got wrong (IB2) lets noise in: at 10% noise 26.3% of IB2's saved instances were noisy; keeping a pass/fail record per case (IB3) fixed it (Hungarian heart IB1 58.7, IB2 55.9, IB3 80.5 with 7.5% stored).
agent_test: Store usage counts (retrieved, helped, harmed) per case and prune by interval, as IB3 does.

claim: Including failures helps only when the memory form can use them. ReasoningBank Shopping: 46.5 to 49.7 with failures; AWM 44.4 to 42.2; Synapse 40.6 to 41.7. Aamodt and Plaza also keep failures for later warnings.
agent_test: Store failures as distilled what-went-wrong items, not raw traces; compare with success-only.
audit_note: Minor: all three method comparisons come from one ReasoningBank ablation (WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash), so 'only when' generalises from one benchmark; Synapse also gained slightly (+1.1).

claim: Distilled strategies beat raw trajectories: ReasoningBank WebArena 48.8 vs Synapse (raw) 42.1 vs AWM 44.1 vs no memory 40.5 (Gemini-2.5-flash); gains hold across three backbones (+8.3, +7.2, +4.6). Gap search qualification: in Hu 2026 distilled Insight memory beats Raw trajectories only across tasks (ALFWorld A to B +6.5 vs -9.5); within one task Raw was better (80.5 vs 65.5). Which wins depends on how far the new task is from the stored one.
agent_test: Compare raw solved-subgoal records with distilled one-line strategies at equal tokens.

claim: Concrete cases and abstract insights help different tasks and are partly complementary. ExpeL gpt-3.5: ALFWorld retrieval-only 55 vs insights-only 50; HotpotQA 31 vs 36; both 59 and 39.
agent_test: Run retrieval-only, insight-only and both arms by task type.

claim: How cases are indexed matters. ExpeL ALFWorld: task-similarity retrieval 59.0, reasoning-similarity 48.5, random successes 42.5, ReAct 40.0 (table row order inferred from a garbled extraction). KATE: nearest-neighbour examples beat random (NQ EM 28.6 to 40.0-41.6) but with a poor encoder TriviaQA fell below random.
agent_test: Compare retrieval keys (problem text, class label, plan summary) for hit rate on held-out same-class problems.
audit_note: Minor: the ExpeL 59.0 row is the full method (insights plus task-similarity retrieval); the ablation compares retrieval rankings within ExpeL.

claim: Human retrieval follows surface similarity, not structure: reminded 52% for surface plus first-order matches vs 7% for pure analogies (Gentner 1993); without comparing two examples spontaneous reuse of an analogue stays near 10 to 30% (Catrambone and Holyoak 1989); richer encoding raised it (Kubricht 2015: animation 81% vs verbal 55%).
agent_test: Probe whether our retriever returns surface-similar but structurally wrong cases; add a structural check at the reuse step.
audit_note: Minor: Gentner 1993 Exp 3 (52% vs 7%) and Kubricht 2015 (55/50/81%, chi-square 6.60) match; Catrambone and Holyoak 1989 could not be downloaded (host unreachable), so the 10-30% range was checked only against its abstract (transfer needs comparison of analogues) and the benchmarks restated in Kubricht (about 10% unaided, about 30% with a dissimilar story).

claim: Part of the gain from retrieved examples is format and label-space priming, not reuse of the solution (random labels cost only 0 to 5% in Min 2022). Gap search: on MATH500, prompts of problems only matched or beat ground-truth solutions (Agarwal 2024); no agent paper has the format-matched irrelevant-case control.
agent_test: Add a control retrieving format-matched but irrelevant cases.
audit_note: Minor: Min 2022 (random labels cost 0-5%, avg 2.6% classification / 1.7% multi-choice) and Agarwal 2024 are about in-context demonstrations on classification/math, so applying them to retrieved agent cases is an inference; KATE shows similar examples still beat random by a wide margin, so priming is only part of the gain.

claim: Models trained on arithmetic behave as case matchers: held-out squares show holes (Llama-2-7B from scratch 30.2% on the held-out square vs 92% random split; GPT-3.5 fine-tuned 97.5% on the square, a small hole). Rule-following fine-tuning reaches over 95% at 12 digits.
agent_test: Not testable by scaffold; suggests stated principles may be needed beside cases.

claim: Gains from reuse depend on how similar the task stream is. Evo-Memory: Pearson r 0.717 (Gemini 2.5 Flash) and 0.563 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) between task similarity and gain. Memento claims +4.7 to +9.6 on out-of-distribution sets, which pulls the other way. Gap search: Hu 2026 cross-task (low similarity) reuse of Raw cases lowered success, which fits the Evo-Memory direction; OBAM shows conflicting near neighbours also harm. No similarity threshold has been measured.
agent_test: Stratify results by similarity of the test item to its nearest stored case; use no memory when similarity is low.

claim: Memory benefits depend on model strength: Dynamic Cheatsheet gains are large for Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o on some tasks, none or harm on others (GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 to 44.0; Claude 3.5 Haiku AIME 2025 no gain over empty scaffold); smaller models cannot curate memory. Gap search: Mallen 2023 adaptive retrieval (retrieve only below a popularity threshold) beat always retrieving by 5.3 points, and plain retrieve-similar-cases memory (Self-StreamICL in the OBAM paper, Claude Sonnet 4) gains +10.9 over zero-shot on DDXPlus (weak zero-shot, 0.753) but only +1.9 on CaseHOLD (strong, 0.788).
agent_test: Test memory use at the model strength we deploy.
audit_note: The +10.9 (DDXPlus) and +1.9 (CaseHOLD) are Self-StreamICL's gains over zero-shot on Claude Sonnet 4 (0.862 vs 0.753; 0.807 vs 0.788), not OBAM's; OBAM's gains over zero-shot are +16.6 and +3.7. Dynamic Cheatsheet figures and Mallen's 5.3-point adaptive-retrieval gain check out.
claim_before_audit: Memory benefits depend on model strength: Dynamic Cheatsheet gains are large for Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o on some tasks, none or harm on others (GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 to 44.0; Claude 3.5 Haiku AIME 2025 no gain over empty scaffold); smaller models cannot curate memory. Gap search: Mallen 2023 adaptive retrieval (retrieve only below a popularity threshold) beat always retrieving by 5.3 points, and OBAM gains are +10.9 on DDXPlus (weak zero-shot) but +1.9 on CaseHOLD (strong).

claim: Self-correction without an external signal fails, so the revise step needs a check. GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after self-correction (Huang 2023); Reflexion helps with external tests (HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1) but MBPP Python false-positive test rate was 16.3% vs 1.4% on HumanEval and MBPP was worse (77.1 vs 80.1). Gap search: Olausson 2024 found self-repair at equal tokens gives marginal gains, with GPT-4 own explanations repairing 33.30% vs 52.60% with human explanations; Kamoi 2024 survey and Stechly 2023 agree.
agent_test: Make every revise step conditional on an executable or independent check; measure the false-pass rate of the check.
audit_note: Minor: Reflexion's unit tests for HumanEval/MBPP are self-generated by the model, with execution as the external signal, which is why the false-positive rate matters; Kamoi 2024 was not re-read beyond its stated findings.

claim: Self-generated cases can replace retrieved ones for large models: GSM8K davinci-003 generated 61 vs retrieved 57; for small models retrieved wins (curie-001 3 vs 2). Sarukkai: the agent's own successful runs, naively retained, lifted ALFWorld 73 to 89 (gpt-4o-mini).
agent_test: Cold-start the case library from the agent's own verified successes before using outside cases.
audit_note: Minor: Yasunaga's 'self-generated' exemplars are model-recalled and unverified, while Sarukkai's are environment-verified successful runs, so the two sources show different things; davinci-002 is a tie (48 vs 47) and only davinci-003 clearly favours self-generation (61 vs 57).

claim: Retrieval-only case use (CBR-RAG) gives small gains where the base model already has parametric legal knowledge: +1.94% cosine (0.8967 to 0.9141, Mistral-7B), 32 test cases; the best setting is significant at 95% against No-RAG and hybrid LegalBERT k=3, and at 90% against hybrid BERT k=1.
agent_test: Skip retrieval when no-memory success is already high.
audit_note: Paper says AnglEBERT k=3 is significant at 95% against both No-RAG and hybrid LegalBERT k=3 (and 90% vs hybrid BERT k=1), not 'only against no-RAG'; other numbers (0.8967, 0.9141, 1.94%, 32 cases, authors attribute high no-RAG score to parametric memory) match.
claim_before_audit: Retrieval-only case use (CBR-RAG) gives small gains where the base model already knows the domain: +1.94% cosine (0.8967 to 0.9141), 32 test cases, significant at 95% only against no-RAG.

claim: Online retention matters: Re4 growing case bank beat a frozen one (+2.75% DCN, +10.08% SP FF1 over CBR+SFT); plain CBR beat SFT alone by about 15 FF1 (64.01 vs 49.46). Single run, in-house 7B model.
agent_test: Test frozen vs growing library on a task stream.

claim: Larger case bases raise retrieval cost and can lower total efficiency past a critical size (utility problem, Minton 1990; Smyth and Cunningham 1996). Review-level claim; no LLM measurement of the analogue (long-context dilution) was read. Gap search: MATH500 in-context accuracy with ground-truth solutions peaks at about 125 examples then declines (Agarwal 2024); uncurated full history gave GPT-4o AIME 2024 6.7 vs 20.0 baseline (Dynamic Cheatsheet); OBAM store-all slightly lowers accuracy.
agent_test: Plot success against library size 10, 50, 250 and look for a peak.
audit_note: Lopez de Mantaras review (utility problem, Minton, Smyth and Cunningham critical case-base size), Agarwal (MATH500 peak ~125) and OBAM match; Dynamic Cheatsheet text says GPT-4o full-history fell to 6.7 vs 20.0 baseline but its Table 2 shows 13.3, an inconsistency inside the paper.

claim: Template-level reuse can give very large gains on puzzle tasks: Buffer of Thoughts Game of 24 GPT-4 3.0 vs 82.4, Checkmate-in-One 36.4 vs 86.4; Dynamic Cheatsheet GPT-4o Game of 24 10 to 99 by storing working code. These are task-family gains, not general ones.
agent_test: Check whether the gain survives when test items are not near-copies of each other.

claim: At counted cost, complex reflect-and-retry loops are not clearly better than plain retry or resampling. HumanEval: no significant accuracy difference between a retry-with-temperature baseline and the best agent, while Reflexion and LDB cost over 50% more and LATS over 50x. Olausson 2024: self-repair at equal tokens gives marginal or no gain with a model's own explanations. Stechly 2023: 15 samples with a sound verifier matched every feedback style (about 40%). No case-library paper reports a cost-matched comparison with an empty-library scaffold.
agent_test: Run the library arm and the empty-library arm at equal total tokens, retrieved text included, and report accuracy per dollar.
audit_note: Kapoor (no significant difference, Reflexion/LDB >50% more, LATS >50x), Olausson (marginal or no gain at equal tokens) and Stechly (15 samples ~40%, comparable to all feedback types) all check out; Stechly's 15-sample arm had no feedback and the sound verifier only scored it.

claim: An explain-the-failure revise step helps only when the explanation is accurate, which needs an outside signal, a stronger explainer or a human. Repair success with GPT-4 own explanations 33.30% vs 52.60% with human ones (Olausson 2024); with the true mistake location, wrong-answer traces gain 18 to 44 points (Tyen 2024), with a random location 5 to 21; the informativeness of feedback made no difference to a sound-verifier loop (Stechly 2023). CHEF-style revise vs plain retry at equal tokens in an LLM has still not been run.
agent_test: Compare plain retry, retry with the raw failure message, and retry with an explanation, all at equal tokens, with the failure signal taken from an executable check.
audit_note: Olausson 33.30% vs 52.60% and Tyen gains (18.04 to 43.92 true location, 5.16 to 21.57 random) and Stechly's null on feedback informativeness all match; 'random 5 to 21' rounds 21.57 down.

claim: False flags have a price. With oracle mistake location, traces whose answer was right lost 0 to 11.43 points on backtracking while wrong traces gained 18.04 to 43.92; random locations cost 6.67 to 15.91 on right traces (Tyen 2024). A judge used to gate retention or revision therefore needs a break-even precision; none has been measured for case retention, and a same-model judge reached about 17% precision on graph colouring (Stechly 2023).
agent_test: Estimate judge precision on our own labels, then compute the break-even from the gain on true flags and the loss on false flags.

claim: Retrieval harm is real and concentrated: on PopQA retrieval turned a right answer into a wrong one on 10% of questions (Mallen 2023); across tasks, Raw trajectory memory cut success on items the agent had failed alone by 26.1 points on ALFWorld (Hu 2026); GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Engineering fell 53.2 to 44.0 with curated memory (Dynamic Cheatsheet); random passages cut accuracy by over 10 points on average (Yoran 2024). No case-memory agent paper reports a harm count per retrieved case.
agent_test: Log, per retrieved case, whether the answer changed from the no-memory answer and in which direction.
audit_note: Mallen 10% (right alone, wrong with retrieval), Hu 2026 Raw memory -26.1 points on ALFWorld baseline-fail instances, Dynamic Cheatsheet GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Engineering 53.2 to 44.0 (DC-Cu is 'cumulative' memory in the paper) and Yoran (random passages cut accuracy by >10 points on average) all match.

claim: A cheap check at the reuse step can prevent harm but costs recall. An entailment (NLI) filter on retrieved passages prevented the loss from irrelevant context but also dropped helpful passages (Yoran 2024). A similarity-plus-code-fingerprint reuse check in a CBR data-science agent passed all 108 retrievals and so never prevented anything (Stocker 2026).
agent_test: Test a structural check (relational match of the case to the new problem) and report both the harm avoided and the helpful cases dropped.

claim: The value of choosing similar cases shrinks as more cases are shown, and accuracy can fall past a point. Banking-77 BM25 advantage over random: 51.5 points at 1 example, 4.9 at 1,500 (Bertsch 2025). MATH500 with ground-truth solutions peaks at about 125 examples then declines (Agarwal 2024). OBAM retrieved-case count saturates at 5. These are classification and maths prompts, not agent case libraries with distractors.
agent_test: Plot success against library size with added distractors at fixed k and at fixed token budget.
audit_note: Bertsch (51.5 to 4.9 points on Banking-77), Agarwal (MATH500 peak ~125 shots then decline) and OBAM (K1 saturates at 5) all match; the claim already flags the scope limit.

claim: A skip-retrieval rule based on what the model already knows beat always retrieving: Mallen 2023 adaptive retrieval 46.5% accuracy, 5.3 points above any non-adaptive method on PopQA; models under 10B parameters gained little because they cannot know when to skip. No agent-level threshold on no-memory success rate has been published.
agent_test: Estimate no-memory success per problem type from a few samples; skip retrieval above a tuned threshold and measure tokens saved and accuracy lost.

claim: Case memory can cost tokens without a score gain. In a CBR data-science agent, prompt tokens rose 49% on Spaceship Titanic (929k vs 625k) for a non-significant gain (0.8147 vs 0.8098), and on NOMAD the score was worse (RMSLE 0.0632 vs 0.0608); 4 seeds each.
agent_test: Report tokens per solved problem for library and empty-library arms.
